title: Inward path close
hookLine: the stations, the diseases, the manners, the virtues: one heart, rusted and polished

cards: A copper pot left in a damp shed goes dull, then green. Nobody did anything to it. It just sat, and the air did the rest.
Bring it inside, rub it with a cloth, and the shine comes back, a patch at a time. The Qur'an uses that picture for the heart.
In surah al-Mutaffifin, in Pickthall's translation: "Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts." Rust can gather. And what gathers can be wiped.

teach.h: THE STATIONS: WHICH WAY TO FACE.
teach.b: Start where the heart days started: the lump of flesh.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says, in paraphrase: in the body is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt.
Truly, it is the heart. Then Jami' at-Tirmidhi explains the rust. In paraphrase: when a servant sins, a black spot is marked on his heart.

If he leaves it, seeks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished. If he returns to it, the spot spreads, and that, the hadith says, is the rust Allah mentions. Now the whole road, through that picture.
The stations, among them repentance, watchfulness, patience, gratitude, reliance, love, sincerity: the way the heart is meant to face.
The diseases: arrogance, envy, showing off, anger, greed, backbiting, lying, heedlessness, despair: the rust itself, named one by one so it can be seen.
The manners, the adab: of speech, eating, guests, travel, sleep, learning, the road and the market, with parents, neighbors, children, animals and the earth: the daily cloth, small wipes.

The virtues: humility, generosity, modesty, truthfulness, pardon, gentleness, justice, ties of kin, loving for others, contentment, and ihsan over all of them: the shine coming back. Not four subjects.
One heart, facing the right way, seeing its rust, wiped daily, and starting to shine.

how: Muslims who follow the inward path work on the heart through repentance, remembrance and good manners, treating the stations, the diseases of the heart and the virtues as one discipline of purifying it.

o: the end of all spiritual effort once the heart is pure
the heart's whole road summed up: rust named, then polished
a closing prayer said at the end of each day's worship

games.q: the inward path — tap the pairs.
p: which way the heart should face
the rust, named one by one

s: the Qur'an speaks of rust upon hearts
al-Mutaffifin 83:14: that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts.
in Tirmidhi's hadith, a black spot can never be removed
if he leaves the sin, seeks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished.
Bukhari's hadith says the whole body follows the heart
if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if corrupt, the whole body is corrupt.

games.q: a black spot has been marked on a servant's heart after a sin. in Tirmidhi's hadith, what polishes it?
o: time; it fades on its own.
leaving the sin, seeking forgiveness and repenting.
games.why: if he leaves it, seeks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished. if he returns, the spot spreads: the rust of 83:14.

practice: Let the road pass by slowly, patience, gratitude, sincerity, gentleness, justice, contentment, the manners of the table and the road, and wait for the one trait you'd most like to be true of you a year from now.
Name it quietly, once, and picture one small wipe of the cloth toward it. If you pray, you can ask Allah for that trait by its name.

wordCard.voice: Inward path close. The stations, the diseases, the manners and the virtues, gathered into one picture: a heart that rusts, and can be polished. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: heart, the one the hadith says the whole body follows.

carryVoice: Your line: polish the heart. What gathers can be wiped. Tomorrow a new block begins: the life cycle.

sources.q: Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts.
